original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: On an admitted one-target unary geometry, do the #4208/#4201 hole mask, the #4169 reverse-word keys and the #4328 repair form one program that restores every payload to the ideal switch and erases its private tapes?
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one quantified implication of #4100 at its caller, prioritizing CRT total repair if that piece is still open. The mask, the reverse word, the repair tariff and the Beneš evaluator already have separate audits. The remaining named step is to run those repair pieces as one program. This package does that for one target. It does not reprice E(p, ell) or claim a new exponent.
bottleneck_link: PR #4100's CRT route restores bad addresses by a keyed sparse repair. Separate audits of the mask, the keys and the tariff do not yet show that the mask tape is what the repair consumes. Closing that ownership join is one caller-bound obligation of the proposed transfer. It does not select a new exponent.
stop_rule: Stop after the one-target ownership join and its failure controls. Do not build a many-target stencil, a Beneš bit-step price for the shears, or a new kappa.
evidence: PROOF.md counts the stencil and applies the permutation lemma to the reverse-word keys. verify.py exhausts 23,040 addresses over five geometries and two sources, checks both invoices, and rejects origin keys, a complemented mask and a target-dependent source. It prints PASS_CRT_JOINED_HOLE_REPAIR.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Cursor Grok, substantial assistance with the proof writeup and the verifier.

open_questions.question: Does a two-target stencil, with disjoint guards, produce the product hole set and restore payloads under the same reverse-word repair?
open_questions.why_it_matters: CRT.md colors several targets in one layer. A one-target join does not show that a second guard block preserves ownership or the permutation.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the unary producer by one more digit block and one more guard block at position J+K, and rerun this repair on every address of one small pair.
open_questions.blocked_by: The #4208 producer emits one target only. This package does not add a second block.

open_questions.question: Is one reverse shear at most the #4377 bit-step budget E(p, ell) = 2^{4 ell}(p+2)^{16} when the control width is the actual H?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This join uses the ten #4169 shears as the key procedure. #4377 prices a different Beneš evaluator. The o(V) repair absorption still needs a bit-step price for these shears.
open_questions.first_step: Expand one modular addition on an H-bit control into head moves in the #4377 bit-step model and compare it with E at H = G = 64(ell + ceil(log2(p+2))).
open_questions.blocked_by: The reverse shears are not expressed as that evaluator's rotation tables, and this package does not translate them.
